deduplication_rule: Any completed GitHub Actions failure where every failed job has no started steps and no job log is the same control-plane/runner-start incident class unless contrary evidence appears.

root_cause.known: The workflow is failing before repository test code starts, so this is not evidence of a WFM product-test defect.
root_cause.unknown: The repository/account-specific trigger remains unconfirmed; likely candidates include runner allocation, Actions entitlement/billing, or another GitHub control-plane restriction.

containment: Treat affected CI as unavailable, not as a product regression.
Do not promote or claim a release from affected runs.
Allow only one bounded retry per new failure fingerprint; repeated identical retries add no evidence.
Keep Railway hosted proof and application health evidence separate from CI control-plane evidence.
Because main is currently unprotected, apply an explicit release freeze while required checks cannot be enforced.
permanent_prevention_rule: A provider-side CI start failure must never be mislabelled as an application failure and must never be bypassed to promote a release. Main must be protected by required independent release checks before release automation is considered reliable.
recovery_verification: A previously failing workflow starts at least one repository-defined step.
A clean run reaches the deterministic test gates.
Branch protection requires the selected release checks before merge or promotion.
safe_change_policy: No production, destructive, tenant-data, or Railway deployment changes are authorised by this incident record.
